weakest_sufficient_contract.name: baseline-relative same-ordinal witness separation
weakest_sufficient_contract.formula: For the fixed baseline row r = R_(n-1), there exists at least one valid alternate row r' in the same ordinal fiber such that r' != r, ordinal(r') = ordinal(r), and identity(r') != identity(r).
weakest_sufficient_contract.why_sufficient: CR14a needs only one constructible alternate stored row identity at the baseline ordinal. Replacing last_row_identity with identity(r') while leaving S.tail=r makes last_row_identity != identity(S.tail) and reaches boundary_link_mismatch; reverting that single field restores RESUME_OK.
weakest_sufficient_contract.why_weaker_than_injectivity: It is existential and baseline-relative. It does not require all distinct same-ordinal rows to have distinct identities, does not require identities to distinguish rows at other ordinals, and does not require global injectivity over the valid-row domain.

stronger_contracts_compared.name: same-ordinal fiber injectivity
stronger_contracts_compared.formula: For every ordinal k and all valid rows x,y with ordinal(x)=ordinal(y)=k, x!=y implies identity(x)!=identity(y).
stronger_contracts_compared.relation: Strictly stronger than needed for CR14a because it universally separates every distinct pair in every ordinal fiber rather than providing one witness for the fixed baseline row.

stronger_contracts_compared.name: global row injectivity
stronger_contracts_compared.formula: For all distinct valid rows x,y, identity(x)!=identity(y).
stronger_contracts_compared.relation: Stronger still; it also separates rows across different ordinals, which CR14a never requires.
